palm-tungsten.name: Palm Tungsten E
@doc: autoSave is false because the OMAP, TSC2102, and Tungsten devices don't save or restore their state yet.
The Tungsten E's OMAP310 runs at 126Mhz, but the CPUARM device counts roughly one cycle per instruction, and
all of the OMAP's timers are derived from the cycle count, so cyclesPerSecond is really the number of instructions
per second of machine time; 32 million is slow enough for most browsers to keep up with in real time.
The input surface is the image of the Tungsten E, and its location array divides it into a 965x1391 grid,
so that the Tungsten device receives image coordinates.
The flash ROM (PalmOS 5.2.1) is at address 0, which is where the CPU starts
addr of 268435456 is 0x10000000, and size of 33554432 is 32Mb of SDRAM
The OMAP310's CPU is a TI ARM925T (ARMv4T)
The touch screen controller (and audio codec) is on uWire chip select 0, and its PINTDAV pin is on GPIO 6
The pen and button regions are positions on the image of the Tungsten E (a 965x1391 scan of a real device),
where each LCD pixel is about 2 image pixels; penHeight is the height of the digitizer in LCD pixels (the LCD
plus the Graffiti area below it).  The power button is on the top edge of a real Tungsten E, so it isn't visible
in the image; its region is the top right corner of the case.
